title: 5 Lead Generation Companies Compared by Scope and Ownership
summary: Compare five lead generation companies by scope, ownership and retained work, with a worked buyer decision and completed acceptance records.
body_markdown:
A proposal for 1,000 contacts and a proposal for ten meetings do not compete on price alone. They leave different work with your team. A useful shortlist starts by naming that work, then checking whether each provider can show how it will be done. Those quantities are illustrative, not benchmarks.


This comparison covers Belkins, SalesRoads, Apollo, Cognism, and Coldreach. They are five options, not a ranking, and they do not all sell the same kind of help. The scope descriptions draw on official-source research dated October 22, 2026, not hands-on testing. Contract terms, asset ownership, and service boundaries require direct confirmation.


Coldreach publishes this blog and is included as an option. Its inclusion is a disclosure, not an independent recommendation.


## 1. Belkins: Outsourced Appointment Setting


[Belkins’ appointment-setting offering](https://belkins.io/appointment-setting) covers outsourced appointment setting, manual research, coordinated email, LinkedIn, and calls, and deliverability management. That scope matters when the work you want to delegate extends beyond supplying names.


The workload under discussion includes finding relevant prospects, coordinating outreach, and managing the sending conditions that support it. A buyer considering this model should ask how those activities connect in the proposed engagement. Research, outreach, and meeting handoff need shared qualification rules.


Your team should still assign an internal owner for targeting decisions, qualification approval, and sales follow-up. Those responsibilities need coverage even when campaign execution is outsourced. Confirm which decisions require your approval and which the provider can make independently.


The precise procurement question is: **“For a meeting to count toward our agreement, what evidence must show account fit, contact relevance, and the prospect’s reason for attending?”**


An appointment-setting description cannot settle that for your business. Put the answer in the scope, including how disputed meetings are reviewed.


## 2. SalesRoads: Managed Dedicated SDR Teams


[SalesRoads](https://salesroads.com/) offers managed dedicated SDR teams, with research, calls, and email in its service scope. It also distinguishes appointment setting from market-research lead-generation outputs. Buyers should preserve that distinction when requesting a proposal.


A managed SDR engagement concerns people, management, and execution. A market-research output can serve a different purpose from a scheduled sales conversation. Ask the provider to specify which workstream it is proposing and how each deliverable will be accepted.


Your team should retain an accountable commercial owner who can explain the offer, approve target segments, and resolve qualification disagreements. Sales capacity also matters: someone must handle the conversations that reach your team. Confirm the proposed division of labor rather than assuming “dedicated team” defines every responsibility.


The precise question is: **“Which deliverables belong to appointment setting, which belong to market research, and what acceptance criteria apply to each?”**


That wording helps prevent research findings, contact records, and meetings from being grouped into one ambiguous lead total.


## 3. Apollo: Connected GTM Data, Intelligence, and Execution


[Apollo](https://www.apollo.io/) is a connected go-to-market platform spanning data, intelligence, and execution. Its AI agents can research, build lists, write outreach, and book meetings. Evaluating it only as a contact database would miss a substantial part of its current scope.


For procurement, the useful question is how much of your workflow the proposed configuration covers. List building, research, message preparation, and meeting booking involve different inputs and approval decisions, even when they happen inside one platform.


Your team should name the owner of targeting rules, agent instructions, message approval, and exception handling. A software capability does not establish that a provider supplies the operating team behind it. Confirm any onboarding, managed support, and ongoing operational responsibilities separately.


The precise question is: **“In our proposed workflow, which actions will agents perform, which require human approval, and where can we inspect the evidence and activity history?”**


Ask for a walkthrough from account selection through meeting handoff, not just a demonstration of individual features.


## 4. Cognism: Sales Intelligence and Contact Data


[Cognism](https://www.cognism.com/) provides sales intelligence, contact data, phone-verified contacts, enrichment, and MCP/API access, with a focus on Europe. It belongs on a shortlist when improving the information available to your sales workflow is a defined part of the purchase.


The workload to scope includes finding relevant records, enriching existing information, and making that information accessible where your team works. Phone verification is a specific data characteristic. It should not be treated as evidence that a person wants a sales conversation.


Your team should identify who owns segmentation, integration decisions, outreach execution, and follow-up unless the agreement explicitly assigns those tasks elsewhere. For European targeting, ask how the proposed data workflow supports your requirements without treating regional focus as a substitute for your own compliance review.


The precise question is: **“For our target markets and required fields, what verification and source context can we inspect, and how will updates reach our operating systems?”**


That ties the evaluation to usable information rather than an undifferentiated record count.


## 5. Coldreach: Account Research Before Outreach


[Coldreach](https://coldreach.ai/) researches accounts for a real reason to reach out before email and LinkedIn outreach. Its AI outbound manager tests signals and angles using lessons from 2,000+ real campaigns run in the last six months.


That campaign experience describes the basis for the testing approach. It is not a promise about your results, and campaign volume does not establish fit for your market.


The workload to examine is the connection between account research and the message sent. Can you see what was found, why it matters to your offer, and how it supports the outreach angle? A plausible fact about an account is not automatically a useful reason to contact it.


Your team should own approval of the commercial proposition and define acceptable evidence, claims, and handoff criteria. Confirm who reviews weak signals and who can change targeting or outreach rules.


The precise question is: **“Show us the research behind an account we know, explain the proposed reason to contact it, and show what happens when the evidence is too weak.”**


## A Practical RFP Checklist


Start with qualification. Define account fit, relevant roles, exclusions, and the conditions that make a conversation worth a salesperson’s time. Give providers examples of acceptable and unacceptable deliverables so they can price and scope the same work.


Separate **booked** , **held** , and **sales-accepted** meetings. Booked means a meeting is scheduled. Held means the conversation occurred. Sales-accepted means your team accepted the conversation against agreed criteria. If you use “sales-accepted opportunity,” specify what additional opportunity requirements apply.


Require source evidence appropriate to the deliverable. For data, ask what verification or provenance is available. For researched outreach, ask to inspect the supporting account evidence. For meetings, ask what record explains qualification and expectations.


Address opt-outs before launch. Specify how objections, unsubscribe requests, and suppression records move between the provider and your systems. Identify who resolves a mismatch so a suppressed contact does not re-enter another campaign.


Write ownership and access terms for domains, mailboxes, platform accounts, campaign data, research, and replies. Ask who registers each asset, who administers it during the engagement, and what remains accessible afterward. Do not infer ownership from whose logo appears on the dashboard.


Define reporting around the purchased work. Records delivered, outreach activity, replies, booked meetings, held meetings, and accepted opportunities should remain distinguishable. Ask how disputed classifications are corrected.


Finally, request written exit terms and a complete fee schedule. Cover setup work, recurring charges, usage credits, additional costs, cancellation obligations, and treatment of unused credits. Specify export formats, transition assistance, and access deadlines without assuming these terms are standard.


## A Worked Buyer Decision: Choose Evidence and Execution


**Everything in this example is invented:** the buyer, suppliers, prices, proposals, source excerpts, people, and activity records. Neither proposal represents any named provider above. These are decision illustrations, not vendor results or market-price benchmarks.


### The buyer’s operating limits


Fictional buyer Larch Systems sells onboarding software to US software companies with 100 to 500 employees. It wants conversations with operations leaders who have a current onboarding bottleneck, not simply companies hiring staff. The pilot lasts eight weeks, with a $12,000 external-spend ceiling. Larch has no SDR and can allocate only two hours weekly to approvals and exceptions. Its account executive can take two discovery meetings weekly. Live calling is not required.


Larch excludes customers, open opportunities, suppressed contacts, and accounts whose apparent problem is already resolved. Before outreach, each included account needs a dated source, an identifiable operational problem, and a relevant role. A hiring announcement alone fails. Sales acceptance requires a held conversation confirming the problem, the contact’s responsibility, and an agreed next step. It does not mean an opportunity has been created.


### Two proposals covering the same eight weeks


**Invented Proposal A, Fieldnote Data: $6,000 fixed total.** It supplies a researched list of 40 accounts, role contacts, source links, and outreach software access. Larch must validate problem evidence, approve messages, operate campaigns, handle replies, and schedule meetings. The proposal assumes six hours of buyer operations weekly. Its sample includes an account because of an older hiring announcement, without checking whether the related operational issue remains open. It promises records and access, not meetings or sales acceptance.


**Invented Proposal B, Cedar Outreach: $11,000 fixed total.** It reviews the same 40-account segment and manages evidence checks, approved email outreach, reply triage, suppression updates, and scheduling during the pilot. Forty accounts are a review ceiling, not a promise to contact all of them. Every rejection gets a reason and source; every inclusion gets evidence supporting the message. Larch retains qualification approval and weekly exception review within its two-hour operating allowance; its account executive owns sales follow-up. Scheduling respects the executive’s capacity. No meeting or opportunity quantity is guaranteed.


Both invented quotes include setup and the stated pilot scope, with no assumed renewal. Both specify buyer-administered sending accounts and a closing export of research, exclusions, activity, and replies. These are fictional negotiated provisions, not claims about any real supplier’s terms. Larch’s owner checks access and the sample export before authorizing launch.


### Decision: approve B, subject to launch checks


Larch selects Cedar Outreach. A fits the cash ceiling but depends on operating time Larch does not have. B includes that execution and, crucially, demonstrates a defensible rejection rather than just a larger list. Its sample checks a hiring signal against newer evidence that the problem has been resolved. A’s sample stops at the signal.


Approval is conditional on the actual pilot using the demonstrated evidence standard, functioning suppression synchronization, and accessible exports. The buyer is not paying a premium for an assumed conversion rate. It is purchasing covered work and inspectable selection decisions within its constraints.


**What reverses the choice?** Choose A if Larch assigns an operator with the required availability and can independently perform the missing evidence checks. Reopen procurement if B cannot reproduce its rejection reasoning or requires more buyer time than agreed. Choose neither if no reviewed account has a supported current problem. Available budget does not justify outreach to weak-fit accounts.


### Completed sample acceptance packet


The following packet is also entirely invented. Source labels refer to fictional documents, not live pages. It records the simulated review at the end of week four, not real campaign performance.


**Selection evidence:**


-


**Included: Alder Cloud, 180 employees.** Fictional source AC-1, a company operations post dated pilot week one, states: “New customers wait for manual workspace provisioning.” Fictional source AC-2 identifies Mira Chen as operations director. The reviewer approves outreach about provisioning delays, not a claim that Alder intends to buy software. CRM customer, opportunity, and suppression checks are clear.


-


**Rejected: Birch Metrics, 220 employees.** Fictional source BM-1, an older hiring post, mentions onboarding expansion. Fictional source BM-2, a newer operations update, states: “Self-service provisioning is live; the onboarding queue is cleared.” The review log marks “problem resolved,” retains both excerpts, and records “no outreach sent.” Fieldnote’s sample had included Birch using BM-1 alone. Cedar’s exclusion is better supported because it considers contrary evidence, not because it has fewer accounts.


**Meeting evidence and disposition:**


-


**Alder: booked, held, sales-accepted.** Fictional log AC-3 records Mira’s reply agreeing to discuss manual provisioning and a calendar acceptance for week three. AC-4 records attendance and notes confirming that delays persist and Mira owns the workflow. AC-5 records the account executive’s acceptance against Larch’s criteria and an agreed technical session. Opportunity creation remains undecided.


-


**Cypress Apps: booked only.** Fictional log CA-1 contains an accepted week-four invitation. CA-2 records a no-show. No conversation notes or sales acceptance exist. The packet marks held “no” and sales-accepted “no,” with rescheduling pending.


-


**Elm Software: booked and held, not sales-accepted.** Fictional logs ES-1 and ES-2 contain the invitation and attendance record. ES-3 records that the attendee cannot confirm an active bottleneck or arrange an introduction to its owner. The account executive rejects acceptance for insufficient qualification. Attendance does not override that finding.


Larch accepts this packet’s classifications, not every meeting as a successful deliverable. The decision rests on traceable inclusion, contrary evidence, and stage-specific records. A calendar entry cannot substitute for any of them.


## Evaluate the Work Your Team Would Retain


If your main requirement is a team making live prospecting calls, ask a human-led service to demonstrate that work. If you already have the operators and need better contact coverage, test data against your actual geography, segment and required fields. If you are evaluating software, assign someone to own targeting and exceptions before comparing automation features.


Coldreach is worth inspecting when account research and the reason behind outreach are central to your buying decision. Ask to see a skipped account alongside an included one, then compare each decision with your own qualification rules.


For broader planning, see our guide to[B2B lead generation](https://coldreach.ai/blog/b2b-lead-generation) . To evaluate Coldreach specifically,[book a demo](https://coldreach.ai/book-a-demo) and ask to inspect the research behind an account you know. Use an account that lets you judge whether the evidence supports the proposed message.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Are these five lead generation companies directly comparable?


Only at a defined scope. They span outsourced execution, managed SDR teams, connected software, and sales intelligence. Ask each provider to address the same business requirement, then document differences in deliverables and remaining internal work.


### Does a booked meeting count as a qualified opportunity?


Not automatically. A booked meeting is a scheduled event. Qualification requires agreed evidence, and opportunity acceptance requires your sales process. Define those stages separately so reporting does not imply progress that has not occurred.


### Who owns the domains, mailboxes, and replies?


The agreement must answer that. Confirm registration, administrative access, usage rights, exports, and post-termination access for each asset. This comparison makes no ownership assumptions about any provider.


### What should we request before signing?


Request a written scope, acceptance criteria, a responsibility split, relevant evidence examples, complete commercial terms, and an exit process. Ask the provider to walk through a hypothetical account from selection to handoff, including exceptions and rejection decisions.
